days.title: Intro to Python, Environment Setup, Variables, Numbers & Text

points.text: A foundational start to get you comfortable with the tools. We will set up your coding environment using Anaconda and Jupyter Notebooks. We'll explore how to write your very first lines of Python, understand basic syntax and indentation, and learn how to run simple interactive commands.

A gentle dive into how Python stores information. We will cover basic data types like integers (whole numbers), floats (decimals), and booleans (True/False). We will also learn how to manipulate text (Strings) and use basic operators to perform simple math and logical comparisons.

days.title: Collections Part 1 & 2: Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries & Sets

points.text: Instead of single variables, learn how to store groups of data. We will focus heavily on Lists (collections that can be added to or modified) and Tuples (collections that are locked). We will clearly explain the crucial concept of "Mutability"—understanding what can and cannot be changed after creation.

We continue our data journey by exploring Dictionaries, which store data in real-world "key-value" pairs (like a contact list). We will also cover Sets, which are perfect for storing unique, non-repeating items. By the end of this session, you will know exactly when to use each data structure.

Time to add logic to our code. We will teach programs how to make choices using simple if, elif, and else conditional statements. Then, we will learn how to completely automate repetitive tasks so you don't have to rewrite code, utilizing for loops, while loops, and the range() function.

Learn to keep your code clean and organized by grouping it into reusable blocks called Functions. We will practice giving functions inputs (parameters) and getting results back (return values). We will also learn how to import helpful, pre-built Python tools (Modules) like math, random, and datetime to make our work much easier.

days.title: Intro to OOP & Next Steps: Inheritance & Magic Methods

points.text: A beginner-friendly introduction to thinking about code as real-world objects. We will strip away the confusing jargon and learn the simple difference between a Class (a blueprint) and an Object (the actual house). We will practice creating simple classes and adding data using the __init__ setup method.

Building gently on our OOP basics, we will learn Inheritance—how a new class can easily borrow code and features from an existing one to save you time. We will briefly touch on how to keep certain data hidden (Encapsulation) and how to use helpful "Magic Methods" (like __str__) so your objects work smoothly with basic commands like print().
